title: Closing the Safety Gap: Surgical Concept Erasure in Visual Autoregressive Models
claim: Fine-tuning a frozen-reference model on auxiliary tokens, with a filtered loss that adjusts only unsafe elements, removes a concept while preserving everything else.
layout: Left-to-right; three stacked VAR streams feeding a large loss module, with legend box
description: A wide left-to-right pipeline diagram. On the far left, two text prompts, a benign one ('A ground on a hill') and an unsafe one ('A church on a hill'), with the key words in blue and red, enter a tall blue Text Encoder. Three horizontal rows follow. Each row has start tokens, multi-scale token maps f1 and f2 in green dashed boxes, and a VAR Visual Transformer. The top two transformers are frozen (blue, snowflake icon) and the bottom one is trainable (orange, flame icon). Each row outputs token maps r1 to r3 in pink, teal or purple. The top outputs feed a KL Loss box that produces L_Pre. The bottom outputs feed a stacked cream panel, 'Filtered CE Loss'. That panel shows token grids with probabilities, a Cross-Entropy block, a diamond threshold check and summation blocks. These produce L_FCE. A dashed legend box in the lower right explains frozen, trainable, forward and not-forward. The eye goes first to the colorful central transformer blocks.
caption: The framework of our method. The left part illustrates the proposed erasure framework adapted for VAR models, while the right part presents the proposed filtered cross entropy loss LF CE and the preservation loss LP re.
abstract: The rapid progress of visual autoregressive (VAR) models has brought new opportunities for text-to-image generation, but also heightened safety concerns. Existing concept erasure techniques, primarily designed for diffusion models, fail to generalize to VARs due to their next-scale token prediction paradigm. In this paper, we first propose a novel VAR Erasure framework VARE that enables stable concept erasure in VAR models by leveraging auxiliary visual tokens to reduce fine-tuning intensity. Building upon this, we introduce S-VARE, a novel and effective concept erasure method designed for VAR, which incorporates a filtered cross entropy loss to precisely identify and minimally adjust unsafe visual tokens, along with a preservation loss to maintain semantic fidelity, addressing the issues such as language drift and reduced diversity introduce by naÃ¯ve fine-tuning. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach achieves surgical concept erasure while preserving generation quality, thereby closing the safety gap in autoregressive text-to-image generation by earlier methods.
